solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Humorous issue that shakes corporation?

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, so the funny outburst that sets the stomach wobbling is a hearty guffaw

explanation.surface: A comic edition of a magazine that rattles a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a business, but it is old slang for a large stomach; 'issue' is something that comes out, here a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, hearty laugh is one that comes from the stomach and makes it shake.

clue.text: Conceited editor to support significant source

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece goes underneath, so the editor comes last

parts.note: big means important or significant
the head of a river is its source

explanation.surface: A vain editor backs an important source of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vain and full of their own importance is described as having a swollen head.

clue.text: Monk touring China comes to island

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the monk goes around the china word

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so pal

explanation.surface: A monk travelling round China reaches an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate, so PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: La Palma is one of the Canary Islands off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Something for sucker picking up ball in game

indicators.note: in a down answer picking up means raising the letters, so they read from bottom to top
in places the ball inside the game word

parts.note: pool is a cue game played on a table
a pill is slang for a ball

explanation.surface: A gullible player gets something while picking up the ball in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' turns POPILLOL upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet on a stick is made to be sucked, so it is something for a sucker.

clue.text: International body and state combine without strings

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
a condition is a state of being
to ally is to join or combine

explanation.surface: A world organisation and a nation join forces with no conditions attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer with no strings attached carries no conditions at all.

clue.text: A king in control — in 1066?

indicators.note: in places the A and king letter inside the control word

parts.note: to have a hold is to have control
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch was in charge during the year of the Norman Conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: England's last Anglo-Saxon monarch reigned until he fell at Hastings in 1066.

clue.text: Chump expected to seize power

indicators.note: seizing means taking hold of, so the word for expected wraps itself round the power letter

parts.note: a train that is expected is due
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A fool is predicted to grab control of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is a gullible fool, the kind of person who is easily tricked or exploited.

clue.text: Green politician in party starts to spout environmental rot

indicators.note: in places the green politician inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
eco is a prefix meaning environmentally friendly
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: An environmentalist MP at a party begins ranting green nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay, the sense of breaking down into constituent parts.

clue.text: Coppers must accept an imposed punishment

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the coins word takes the article inside

parts.note: copper coins are pennies, so coppers gives pence

explanation.surface: Police officers have to accept a penalty handed out to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police, but means copper coins, PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A penance is a punishment undertaken or imposed to atone for a wrong.

clue.text: Attempt by government to leak information

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt
public as in the public sector, the realm run by the state

explanation.surface: A ministry tries to slip secrets to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Revealing something previously secret to everyone is the idiom for making it known openly.

clue.text: Nation embraces popular French playwright

indicators.note: embracing is holding something within one's arms, so the nation word goes round the popular word

parts.note: a race can mean a nation or people
something popular is in, fashionable

explanation.surface: A country takes a well-liked French dramatist to its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Dad abandons Spanish dish for this woman

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving, so the dad word walks out of the dish and leaves the rest

parts.note: paella is the rice dish of Valencia
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A father walks out on a Spanish meal and goes off with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's name, so it can stand for any woman named in a clue.

clue.text: Newspaper article by Belgian writer

parts.note: the i is a British national newspaper
an is the indefinite article
a Fleming is a Flemish-speaking Belgian

explanation.surface: A piece in the paper written by an author from Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper' is the i, a British daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator of James Bond was a British novelist and journalist.

clue.text: Doing as ordered one's reaching conclusion

indicators.note: being put in order means the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: one is I, and 's is the S of 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone who does as they are told comes to the end of a task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges DOING AS into DIAGNO; 'one's' is I plus 'S, as in one is.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's diagnosis is the judgement reached after examining a patient's symptoms.

clue.text: Teacher beginning to grumble about head

indicators.note: the beginning is the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: over means about, as in arguing over money
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher starts complaining about the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A governess is a woman employed to teach children in a private household.

clue.text: Spiked wheel — gardening tool saving time?

indicators.note: saving is used in its old sense of except, so the tool is taken without the time letter

parts.note: a trowel is a small hand tool for digging

explanation.surface: A spiky wheel that is a garden tool which saves effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like economising, but here it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small revolving toothed disc at the end of a rider's spur.

clue.text: What falls easily to one as Northerner?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, a ... is something that lands in one's lap, a windfall
someone from the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Something that comes easily to a person from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Lapland, the Arctic region of northern Scandinavia, is a northerner.

clue.text: Regular myth, exploded, set in rich ground

indicators.note: set in places the exploded letters inside the other group
ground means crushed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged
blown apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A common legend, shattered, is buried in fertile soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich' reads as fertile and 'ground' as soil, but 'ground' means crushed: both words are anagram signals, and 'set in' nests one jumble inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhythmic beat repeats at regular intervals, steady and even.

clue.text: Republican in disreputable club shows ambition

indicators.note: in places the party letter inside the club word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub

explanation.surface: A politician seen in a seedy nightspot reveals his ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive is ambition or determination, the urge to get ahead.

clue.text: Chemical substance spy used against sappers?

indicators.note: against means next to, so the spy sits beside the sappers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A chemical weapon an agent deployed against military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used in a chemical reaction to detect or produce others.

clue.text: Unwind the flexes with plug in

indicators.note: flexing bends and twists, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: An electrician uncoils the cables with the plug connected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexes' looks like electric cables, but it is the anagram signal working on THE PLUG IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax and stop being so serious or tense is the phrasal-verb sense of unwinding.

clue.text: New on street, work without break

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A newcomer on the road works without a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Something continuous with no pause or interruption runs right through.

clue.text: Spots food in dining room — no starter provided

indicators.note: in places the food inside the shortened dining room word
no starter means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a mess is where soldiers or officers eat
a pie is a baked dish of food

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the mess hall serves no first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no starter' drops the first letter of the dining-room word; 'provided' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so the third-person form means spots.

clue.text: Untouchable carcass not to be moved

indicators.note: letters that are moved shift position, so these get rearranged

explanation.surface: A dead body that must not be shifted from where it lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred or beyond criticism cannot be interfered with, hence untouchable.

clue.text: Tongue forming content of metal container

indicators.note: the contents are what is inside, so the outer letters of the container are dropped

parts.note: a tin can holds food or drink

explanation.surface: A language takes shape inside a metal tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' keeps the inside of TIN CAN, dropping the outer T and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Inca is used for Quechua, the language of the Inca empire in the Andes.

clue.text: Arab sycophants shunning second one

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the second letter is cast out of the flatterers

parts.note: yes-men agree with everything the boss says
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Arab boss gets rid of one of his toadies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunning' removes S from YES-MEN to give YEMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Yemen, a country on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab.

clue.text: Mourned day after soldiers brought in dead

indicators.note: after puts the day letter at the end, following the rest
bringing in places the soldiers inside the word for dead

parts.note: the late king means the dead king
men are ordinary soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A day after troops carried in the fallen, they were grieved over.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament someone is to grieve for them, so the past tense is mourned.

clue.text: Love missing husband, not that she regrets

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the husband letter goes from the word

parts.note: this, not that: the opposite pointing word

explanation.surface: A lover whose husband has gone missing says that is not what she regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Cole Porter's song 'Miss Otis Regrets'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's song has Miss Otis sending regrets she is unable to lunch today.

clue.text: Junk entering island by river — Hong Kong feature?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the river letter sits alongside at the end
entering means going into, so the junk word goes inside the island

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides
scrap is junk, waste material

explanation.surface: A Chinese sailing junk enters an island harbour near a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junk' suggests the Chinese boat to fit Hong Kong, but it means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hong Kong's skyline is famous for its very tall buildings, so one is a characteristic sight there.
